doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Joining Hot Chocolate and early recording
summary: After a research degree he joined Hot Chocolate for two years; he had recorded with the Monty Python team in 1973 while still at university.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So you had a free ticket at a university yet if this is correct you gave it up to go with Hot Chocolate? Is that correct?

That was a couple of years later. I came back to London and was doing a research degree and then I got a phone call asking if I’d like to join the group Hot Chocolate who at the time were the number one singles band after The Beatles. And I don’t know if I thought — well that’s my next profession or anything like that. I thought oh that would be fun to do a year or a tour or a couple of tours with them, which it turned out to be two years of great fun.
Did you find that in that situation you kept getting asked to do more things and you just figured out how to do them?

Pretty much, yes. Because looking back now it’s very interesting because it’s all around the same time I’d done some playing — I started recording when I was 19 which seems ridiculous because I was still at University.
